extracted.intended_audience: pipeline operators, pipeline safety compliance officers, industry stakeholders, and state/federal pipeline safety regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and performance standards for installing rupture-mitigation valves (RMVs) or alternative equivalent technologies and for identifying, isolating, and responding to pipeline ruptures on newly constructed or entirely replaced onshore gas transmission, Type A gathering, and hazardous liquid pipelines (≥6 in.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability (pipelines covered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies to most newly constructed and entirely replaced onshore gas transmission, Type A gas gathering, and hazardous liquid pipelines with diameters of 6 inches or greater; includes certain regulated hazardous liquid gathering lines (e.g., regulated rural hazardous liquid gathering pipelines crossing bodies of water >100 feet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'entirely replaced' as 2 or more miles being replaced with new pipe within any stretch of 5 contiguous miles within any 24-month period. The rule generally omits offshore pipelines, smaller-diameter pipelines, and certain gathering lines unless specifically called out. See exemptions for specific pipeline classes and gathering line types elsewhere in the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to install rupture-mitigation valves (RMVs) or alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must install rupture-mitigation valves (ASVs or RCVs) or demonstrate installation of alternative equivalent technologies on pipelines subject to the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RMVs include automatic shut-off valves (ASV) and remote-control valves (RCV). The rule codifies installation, spacing, operation, and maintenance requirements for these devices on covered pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance standard for alternative equivalent technologies (30-minute isolation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative equivalent technologies must meet the performance standard for RMVs, including the ability to immediately enable isolation of a rupture — in 30 minutes or less, measured from an operator's identification of a rupture after notification of a potential rupture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHMSA will review notifications seeking to use alternative equivalent technologies and requires demonstration that the alternative provides an equivalent level of safety (see notification criteria). 'Immediately enable isolation' is operationalized as full segment isolation ≤30 minutes after rupture identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notification and demonstration for alternative technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators seeking to install alternative equivalent technologies must submit a notification to PHMSA in advance of installation demonstrating equivalent level of safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstration should reference technical and safety factors including, but not limited to: design, construction, maintenance, and operating procedures; technology design and operating characteristics such as operation times (closure times for manual valves); service reliability and life; accessibility to operator personnel; nearby population density; and potential consequences to the environment and the public. For manual valves used as alternatives, the notification must also demonstrate economic, technical, or operational infeasibility of RMV installation by referencing factors like access to communications and power; terrain; prohibitive cost; labor and component availability; ability to secure land access rights and permits; and accessibility for installation and maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve spacing requirements (class-location-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes valve spacing thresholds including maximum spacing of no more than 8 miles in Class 4 locations and 15 miles in Class 3 locations for RMVs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHMSA also establishes spacing thresholds within and outside HCAs and provides valve spacing limits for highly volatile liquid (HVL) pipelines in populated areas. Specific spacing requirements depend on pipeline type, commodity, class location, and risk analysis; check section-by-section provisions (§§ 192.634/195.418/195.260 etc.) for exact numeric and situational rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure timeframe for RMVs and alternatives (rupture isolation time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must respond to an identified rupture by closing RMVs or alternative equivalent technology to provide complete valve shut-off and segment isolation as soon as practicable, but no more than 30 minutes after rupture identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rupture isolation time is defined as the time from operator identification of a rupture after notification of potential rupture, through implementing response procedures, to fully closing appropriate valves to terminate the uncontrolled flow. The 30-minute limit is an absolute maximum; operators are expected to minimize isolation time in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rupture identification and 'notification of potential rupture' procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires a definition of 'notification of potential rupture' and establishment of written procedures for identifying and responding to a rupture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Notification of potential rupture' identifies signs of an uncontrolled release of a large volume of commodity observed by or reported to the operator. Operators must establish written procedures that describe how to identify potential ruptures (e.g., alarms, SCADA/flow/pressure indications, third-party reports) and steps to confirm and respond, consistent with §§ 192.635/195.417 and associated sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve status monitoring and control capability
rubrics_metrics.description: RMVs and alternative equivalent technologies must be capable of having their status controlled or monitored remotely (directly, or indirectly via upstream/downstream pressure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ASVs, an operator does not need to monitor remotely a valve's status if the operator can monitor pressures or gas flow rate on the pipeline to identify and locate a rupture. Alternative technology segments must have the capability to monitor pressures or flow rates to identify and locate a rupture. Monitoring can be direct valve status telemetry or inferred from pipeline sensors (SCADA, flow/pressure transmitters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance, inspection, and drills for RMVs and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must perform maintenance and inspection on RMVs and alternative equivalent technologies; maintenance includes drills for alternatives that are manually or locally operated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintenance programs must ensure reliability and operability. Drills should exercise manual or local procedures to ensure personnel can achieve required closure times. See § 192.745/195.420 and section-by-section analysis for inspection, testing, and maintenance intervals and recordkeeping requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-event reviews and incorporation of lessons learned
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must perform post-event reviews of incidents, failures, or other events involving closure of RMVs or alternative equivalent technologies and incorporate lessons learned into personnel training, qualifications, and into design, construction, testing, maintenance, operations, and emergency procedures and specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-event reviews should evaluate whether performance objectives were met, identify root causes, and document corrective actions to be applied system-wide. These reviews support continuous improvement and regulatory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency response plans: immediate 9-1-1 notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires operators to update emergency response plans to ensure immediate and direct contact of appropriate public safety answering points (9-1-1 emergency call centers) or coordinating government officials upon notification of a potential rupture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to pipelines subject to the emergency planning requirements (e.g., §§ 192.615 and 195.402). The intent is immediate direct notification to local emergency services to accelerate public safety response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remediation, interim measures, and timelines for inoperable RMVs
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RMV or alternative equivalent technology is found inoperable or cannot maintain shut-off, operators must repair or replace it as soon as practicable and may need to install an alternative compliant valve within 7 calendar days of the finding while repairs are made, documenting an interim response plan to maintain safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative compliant valves installed temporarily are not required to meet valve spacing requirements of the part. Operators must document remediation steps, timelines, and interim safety measures and follow notification procedures when seeking exemptions or deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions and conditional applicability (Class locations, gathering lines, and segment replacement thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain pipelines and situations are exempt or treated differently: RMV requirements do not apply to gas transmission and Type A gas gathering pipeline segments in Class 1 or Class 2 locations with a potential impact radius (PIR) ≤ 150 feet; Type B and Type C gas gathering pipelines are exempt; replacements <1,000 feet within any mile (24-month period) are exempt; operators replacing between 1,000 feet and 2 miles may either install RMVs or automate existing valves with actuators and pressure sensors (max spacing 20 miles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulated rural hazardous liquid gathering pipelines are required to install RMVs or equivalents only where they cross bodies of water >100 feet in width from high water mark to high water mark. When class location changes trigger replacement of ≥2 miles within 5 contiguous miles, operators must install/modify valves to meet spacing and rupture mitigation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFRD (Emergency Flow Restricting Device) determination and required factors
rubrics_metrics.description: If an operator determines an EFRD is needed on a segment that is located in, or could affect, an HCA, the operator must install the EFRD and evaluate specific factors in making that determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors to evaluate include: swiftness of leak detection and pipeline shutdown capabilities; type of commodity; rate of potential leakage; volume that can be released; topography or pipeline profile; potential for ignition; proximity to power sources; location of nearest response personnel; specific terrain within the HCA or between the pipeline segment and the HCA it could affect; and benefits expected by reducing spill size. EFRD location, installation, actuation, operation, and maintenance must meet applicable RMV and rupture-mitigation requirements (e.g., §§ 195.258, 195.260, 195.402, 195.418, 195.419, and 195.420).

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve installation and spacing obligations after class-location-driven replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: For gas pipelines where the operator, in response to a class location change, chooses to replace ≥2 miles of pipe within a contiguous 5 miles, the operator is required to install or modify valves as necessary to comply with the valve spacing and rupture mitigation requirements of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators replacing between 1,000 feet and 2 miles get additional flexibility (install RMVs or automate existing valves with actuators and pressure sensors, maximum spacing 20 miles). Replacements less than 1,000 feet within any single mile during any 24-month period do not trigger RMV installation/spacing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASV specific performance and testing requirement (shut‑in pressure verification)
rubrics_metrics.description: An operator using an ASV as an RMV must document and confirm ASV shut-in pressures on a calendar year basis not to exceed 15 months; ASV shut-in set pressures must be proven and reset individually at each ASV at least each calendar year but at intervals not to exceed 15 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation is required in accordance with § 195.419(f). This annual/15-month verification ensures valves operate at designed shut-in pressures and remain effective for rupture mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak detection and pipeline monitoring capability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Pipeline segments using alternative equivalent technology or relying on ASV operation must have the capability to monitor pressures or gas flow rates on the pipeline to identify and locate a rupture (e.g., LDS, SCADA, flow/pressure transmitters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHMSA references design and operational requirements for computational pipeline monitoring (CPM) leak detection systems (§ 195.134 and § 195.444) and requires LDS for pipelines in or that could affect HCAs (§ 195.452(i)(3)). Monitoring capability can substitute for direct remote valve status monitoring when it provides equivalent rupture identification and location information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve capability requirements (operation times, reliability, maintainability)
rubrics_metrics.description: RMVs and alternative technologies must have operational characteristics suitable for rupture mitigation, including acceptable operation/closure times, service reliability and life, accessibility to personnel, and ability to maintain shut-off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When seeking to use alternatives or manual valves, operators must demonstrate via notification that the alternative's operation times, reliability, accessibility, and other characteristics provide an equivalent level of safety compared to RMVs. Closure times and reliability are central to meeting the 30-minute isolation performance objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation, recordkeeping, and notification procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must document equivalence demonstrations, maintenance and testing records, ASV shut-in verification, interim response plans for inoperable RMVs, and use PHMSA notification procedures where exemptions or infeasibility claims are made (e.g., § 195.18 / § 192.18).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications for alternative technologies, exemption requests, and demonstrations of infeasibility must follow the rule's notification procedures and provide the technical evidence and rationale specified (design, operational constraints, economic/technical infeasibility factors, etc.). Proper documentation supports PHMSA review and compliance enforcement.
